VINIT.chosen_element: Uninitialized scalar field Z/qZ before any key material exists
VINIT.justification: The void state before a private key scalar n is chosen from the curve order q; no point has been mapped, no generator applied, the field is empty of cryptographic content.

TANCH.chosen_element: The secp256k1 curve order q and the curve equation y²=x³+7
TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor is the cyclic group structure of order q on the curve; it bounds the entire system by defining the finite field F_p, the curve equation, and the generator point G that closes the loop between scalar and point.

AFWD.chosen_element: Scalar multiplication n×G mapping secret key to public key
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism is the deterministic, efficient transformation from the private scalar n to the public point P=(x,y) on the curve; this is the easy direction of the trapdoor binding.

AREV.chosen_element: Discrete logarithm problem: recovering n from P
AREV.justification: The reverse morphism attempts to descend from the public point P back to the secret scalar n; this is computationally infeasible, representing the hard direction of the trapdoor binding.

CLINK.chosen_element: Composition of scalar multiplication with curve point addition
CLINK.justification: The composition operator chains the scalar multiplication n×G through the group law of the curve, linking the private key generation, the point computation, and the public key output in a sequential morphism.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The generator point G as the identity reference for all scalar multiplications
IMSCRIB.justification: The generator G is the self-referential base point that every scalar multiplication starts from; it is the identity element of the group and the canonical reference that makes n×G well-defined.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The public key point P=(x,y) splitting into its x-coordinate and y-coordinate components
FSPLIT.justification: The public key point on the curve splits into two distinct coordinate branches: the x-coordinate in F_p and the y-coordinate in F_p, each carrying partial information about the point but neither sufficient alone to recover the secret.

FFUSE.chosen_element: Reconstruction of the point P=(x,y) from its coordinate components
FFUSE.justification: The two coordinate branches fuse back into the single point P on the curve; the pair (x,y) must satisfy y²=x³+7 to reconstruct the original public key point, recovering exactly what was split.

EVALT.chosen_element: Successful verification that P=n×G holds for a given n and P
EVALT.justification: The affirmative branch confirms that the scalar multiplication of the secret key n with the generator G produces the claimed public key P, validating the trapdoor binding.

EVALF.chosen_element: Failed discrete logarithm attempt: no n found such that n×G=P
EVALF.justification: The negative branch represents the failure state where the discrete logarithm problem cannot be solved; no scalar n can be recovered from the public point P within feasible computation.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Simultaneous holding of both the public point P and the unrecoverable secret n
ENGAGR.justification: The paradice state holds both the public key point P (which is known) and the secret scalar n (which is computationally hidden) simultaneously without resolution; the system exists in both states at once.

IFIX.chosen_element: Permanent recording of the public key point P on the curve
IFIX.justification: The public key P is fixed as a permanent, append-only record on the elliptic curve; once computed and published, it cannot be undone or altered, serving as the immutable output of the key generation process.
